definitions.meaning: a machine that breaks down or fails is said to pack up or conk out
to deal cards or rations is to hand them round

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their job in order to strike a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A failing engine is said to give out, and handing out cards or supplies is dealing them.

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'
a spare is a reserve kept in case of need

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper but has stamina in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: GO SPARE is British slang for becoming extremely angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Going spare is British slang for flying into a rage.

clue.text: Relatives turning out to be resourceful

indicators.note: the letters are turned about and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Family members prove handy in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versatile adapts to many tasks, so is inventive and capable.

indicators.note: the letters are made new by being put into a fresh order

parts.note: the word depot, with 's as 'is' linking it to the definition

explanation.surface: A freshly built warehouse has been selected.
explanation.definitionFit: Having opted for something is having selected or picked it.

parts.note: a tech is a technical college

indicators.note: the head of the next word, its first letter, leaves it

parts.note: singular in the sense of one of a kind, unique

explanation.surface: A school principal departs from a remarkable building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head's leaving' removes the first letter of UNIQUE, leaving NIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility means skill or ease of performance, which is what good technique gives.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Political

parts.note: reckoning up a sum is adding

explanation.surface: A party leader is counting on some form of cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Political leader' looks like a named politician, but 'leader' only takes the first letter, P; 'on' simply joins it to ADDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is soft material used as cushioning or protection.

clue.text: Outstanding union leader involved in stimulus to action

indicators.note: the first letter is placed inside the word for a stimulus

parts.note: a prod is a poke or nudge that spurs someone on

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of union

explanation.surface: A notable trade unionist is caught up in pushing for strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union leader' looks like a trade unionist but gives only U, put inside PROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean projecting above a surface, standing out, as a nail head stands proud.

clue.text: He takes risks with crazy road speed

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the two words go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A reckless driver goes at an insane pace on the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw ready for any danger.

clue.text: Spanish artist's upset about one epic work

indicators.note: the turned name goes round the letter for one
in a down clue upset turns the painter's name upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Salvador Dalí was a Spanish surrealist painter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Spanish painter is distressed over a single great piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is the reversal signal, apt in a down clue where the name is turned upside down; 'about' then wraps the turned name round the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is the classic epic poem of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Bitterness before one scuppered old ship

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes before, above, the second

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour

indicators.note: scuppered means wrecked, so the letters of one are wrecked and reordered

explanation.surface: Resentment comes before someone sinks an ancient vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scuppered' suits a ship but here signals the anagram of 'one'; 'before' places the bitterness word above it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the 15th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: Race without pole that's part of the rigging

indicators.note: without tells us to leave out the pole's letter from the race word

parts.note: a sprint is a short fast race
N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: A race held with no pole, something belonging to a ship's ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is a magnetic pole, North, giving N, removed from SPRINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprit is a spar running diagonally to extend a sail, a piece of a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Go over account given by flyer

parts.note: to cross a road is to go over it
a bill is an account of money owed

explanation.surface: Someone checks an invoice handed over by a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbill is a finch with crossed mandibles, a bird and hence a flyer.

clue.text: Agreed to split a company and left

indicators.note: one word goes into the middle of the other, splitting it apart

parts.note: a band is a company of musicians or soldiers
saying 'done!' signals that a deal is agreed

explanation.surface: A business partnership is broken up by agreement and the partner walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: DONE goes inside A BAND, after A BAN, to give A BAN DONE D.
explanation.definitionFit: Left in the sense of deserted: a place that has been left has been forsaken.

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
what is due to you is your right

explanation.surface: Someone supplies instructions and declares them correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions' are two compass points, E and N, and DUE is a noun for what one is entitled to.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is an old verb meaning to invest or endow someone with a quality.

clue.text: Backing struggle headed by English poet

indicators.note: in an across clue the piece that heads another stands in front of it
backing means the word for struggle is read from right to left

parts.note: to toil is to labour or struggle

explanation.surface: Supporting a fight led by an English writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns TOIL into LIOT, which E then heads.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot, author of The Waste Land, is one of the best-known modern poets writing in English.

clue.text: Town agreed to joining the northern link

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
something agreed is on, as in 'the deal is on'
a bridge links two places

explanation.surface: A town agrees to connect to the north by a new crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire and other northern English speech 'the' is clipped to t'. TONBRIDGE is a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a market town in Kent, south-east England.

parts.note: a quota is a share or allotted portion; the 's stands for 'has'

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A stock is shifting into place in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges INTO as TION, added to QUOTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotation is a line or passage cited from a book or speech.

parts.note: an outgoing person is sociable and friendly

explanation.surface: Spending by a mutual benefit club.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly society is a British mutual insurance club, but here 'friendly' and 'society' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are the sums of money paid out, so costs or spending.

indicators.note: translation turns the words into a different form, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: Something matches a version rendered in local speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things are exactly alike, the same in every respect.

parts.note: read as open countryside: a protected ring of undeveloped land around a town, the shared open space a planning policy keeps

explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is a zone of open countryside around a city where building is restricted, land held for the general good.

parts.note: an estate is a British estate car, a station wagon, and these are buildings that house cars

explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate' suggests a housing estate, but it is an estate car, the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is a building where a car, estate or otherwise, is kept.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people also have faith in omens.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped marks used in printing as reference signs.

definitions.meaning: a law that is valid is operative and binding
servicemen are serving in the armed forces, enlisted there

explanation.surface: A legitimate post for military personnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule currently operative is in force, and those who serve are in the forces.

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crewed by eight oarsmen, so a member of that crew

explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is crewed by eight oarsmen, each pulling one oar.

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

explanation.surface: A woman's purchases of bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like prices but is the slang 'rap', an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wraps are shawls or coverings, and blankets is a fair plural synonym.

clue.text: Idea related to partly formed intention

parts.note: an idea is a thought
of signals belonging or relation, as in 'the colour of the sky'

explanation.surface: A notion connected with a half-made plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a phrase: something merely considered, as in 'I had thought of leaving', is a plan half-formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something you have considered but not decided on is a tentative plan, not yet a firm resolve.

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the pair of words is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: dim means slow-witted
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth orders

explanation.surface: A foolish Italian is overly careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DIM IT as one run into TI MID.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person is fearful and shy, so wary and careful.

definitions.meaning: the national police force of the Republic of Ireland
a large lake in northern Italy

explanation.surface: Irish officers spotted beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is Ireland's police force, and Lake Garda is Italy's largest lake.

clue.text: Soldiers using guns made originally to protect king

indicators.note: the shuffled letters wrap round and shield the king's letter
the words are given in an original, freshly invented arrangement

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Troops guarding the monarch with weapons built in-house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' signals the anagram of 'guns made', and 'to protect' has the shuffled letters surround the king's R, fitting the soldiers' guarding role.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardsmen are soldiers of a regiment of guards, such as the British Foot Guards.

clue.text: He moves fast to rally resistance

parts.note: a car rally is a kind of race
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A man hurries off to drum up opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rally' looks like a verb for gathering support, but it is a motor rally, a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is anyone who competes at speed, such as a runner or driver.

indicators.note: the word for exhaust is broken open so another word can sit inside it

parts.note: to exhaust resources is to spend them
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A car's damaged exhaust pipe holds up the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like a car part but is the verb, used up: SPEND, broken by US.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend proceedings is to put them off or hold them over, a postponement.

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
feeling down is feeling blue

explanation.surface: Diluting paint makes a shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water down' reads as one verb, to dilute, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea blue is a shade of greenish blue like the ocean's.
